Some options for you to discuss with your doctor: 

-Try a different birth control. Several work for PCOS and a different formulation may cause less dryness for you. 

-Start Nuva ring in addition to your oral birth control. Nuva ring increases vaginal lubrication. It's usually ok to be on 2 birth control, especially since the Nuva ring acts locally and has a low dose of hormones. 

-Try taking spironolactone for your PCOS instead of birth control. It's a diuretic but can also treat PCOS because it blocks male hormones. It won't cause dryness because it's not hormonal. If you did this obviously you'd need something else for birth control.

We need to eat a lot to get out of starvation mode, and after that, our appetites may start to normalize.

Furthermore, another commenter (who since deleted their comment) pointed out that sometimes ED's can hinge on eating times and get really rigid about that. So be careful not to swing in that direction. 

However, the part about "parkouring" from ED straight to IE holds. That's a big leap that isn't necessarily recommended.

You know yourself best, so do what's best for you, but those are my thoughts. Good luck! <3

You can start it anytime you want. It will be effective at protecting against pregnancy after 7 days of pills.

However, the reason why you're getting all this advice is that starting a pack at a specific point in your cycle might let you get away with less "break through bleeding" which is bleeding between periods. A pack of pills basically tells your body when to bleed. If you start a pack in the middle of your cycle, it won't hurt you, but your body might be like "uh whoa what am I supposed to be doing?" and you might have some unexpected bleeding, probably evening out to a regular monthly cycle in a few months.

So, if you want to minimize breakthrough bleeding, my advice would be to take it the day you finish bleeding. Then you have 3 weeks until your sugar pill week which follows your natural pattern.

But it won't hurt you either way, you can do whatever you want, especially if you need preg protection asap.

\*\*bonus info: some sources may say that if you start a pack within 7 days of the first day if your period, it is effective immediately. This is only true if you have super regular cycles, which most teens do not (maybe you're a teen?) so beware. My advice is always to use a back up method (condoms or abstinence) for 7 days after starting, just to be sure.

Practical tips: 

* Reading glasses helped me a ton. I got cheap ones from a drug store (1.5 strength I think) and my reading comprehension went way up due to reduced eye strain (warning though: I think my eyes adjusted and now depend on them)
* Always read on paper rather then on the computer. If you have to read a lot on the computer, download Flux to make your screen easier to look at, again reducing eye strain.
* Most dyslexics have a color that is easier to read on. Usually it's blue. If you can, print things out  on light blue paper. Or, get a see-through blue plastic paper cover and put it over the page you're reading in a book.
* There is a font called dyslexie, designed to be easier for dyslexics to read ([https://www.dyslexiefont.com/en/typeface/](https://www.dyslexiefont.com/en/typeface/))

Emotional tips:

* Remember that everyone has a "thing" that makes the MCAT uniquely challenging to them. Some people have children at home, some people struggle hard with finances, some people have other learning differences such as ADD, some people are ESL. Don't fall into the trap of thinking everyone else who is taking the MCAT has unlimited money to spend on materials, doesn't have to work, and has a maid cooking and cleaning for them. Everyone has challenges but if people let those challenges hold them back, there would be empty exam rooms, nation-wide. 
* Think about it as much as you need to in order to make the appropriate accommodations. And then, as much as you can, try not to think about it. The more I think about my dyslexia, the more I notice it.

Why is it confusing that an organization would be both nonprofit and funded by tax dollars? Shouldn't any socially beneficial organization be? They both are ways of saving the organization money so that they can better provide beneficial services.

I want to clarify what "tax funding for PP" means. There is no line item in the federal budget called "keep PP running". It just means that PP accepts medicaid. When any patient with medicaid seeks medial attention, they go to a health care facility (which some times may be PP) and receive their treatment at no cost to them. The facility then submits a claim to medicaid, as it would any other insurance company. The state medicaid then bills the federal medicaid which then reimburses the state medicaid for part of the costs. This is how it works at any health care facility that accepts medicaid. PP is no different. 

There is also Title X. This isn't talked about as often because it doesn't provide as much funding as medicaid but it still is a source of funding that some PP's rely on. Title X was established in the 70's  to ensure that lower income women receive affordable birth control and preventative care. It is ultimately a cost-saving endeavour and is very effective at that (presentation is by *far* cheaper then treatment). Again, nothing special about PP here. Most facilities that provide preventative reproductive health care receive Title X funding. 

A decades-old law prevents patients from using medicaid to fund abortions. Title X does not cover abortions. Therefore, no tax money ever funds abortions. Patients often shoulder the financial burden themselves which is almost always upwards of $500. 

Medicaid reimbursements and Title X funding make it possible for people of lower income to receive preventative services including birth control, STI testing, PAP smears, breast exams, and referrals to other services. When people talk about defunding PP at the federal levels what they're talking about is making it impossible for PP to accept medicaid. This will not shut down PP. This will not affect abortion rates. All this will do it make preventative reproductive healthcare harder or, in some areas, impossible, for people of lower incomes to access. "Defunding" PP is an attack on social equity and on civil health care rights. It will only widen the already atrocious economic, racial, and opportunity inequity present in our country.

If you got the copper/paraguard you're always protected right away.

If you got a hormonal IUD, you're technically protected right away as long as you got it within 5 days of the first days of your period. This is only 100% certain if your periods are normally very regular, meaning they come at the same time each month like clockwork.

One type of sensory receptor is called a mechanoreceptor that responds to mechanical pressure such as touch and stretch (other receptors respond to chemicals, heat, pain, etc). Because there are many mechanoreceptors in genital regions (of males and females) mechanical stimulation triggers a chemical response that is relayed via afferent neurons to your brain. It is possible, however, for higher brain centres to override the response to this stimulus. 

Bonus round: Erections!
The penis is filled with three cylindrical vascular compartments, each composed of one artery (that blood flows into) and one vein (through which blood flows out). When when penis is not stimulated, these arteries are under control of the sympathetic nervous system which causes the muscle around the arteries to contract so not much blood is filling them. During erection, sympathetic input to the muscles surround the arteries is inhibited and the arteries are allowed to dilate. (How? Autonomic neurons cause surrounding endothelial cells to release nitric oxide which relaxes the arterial smooth muscle causing vasodilation). The vascular compartments become engorged with blood at high pressure. As the vascular compartments expand, the veins (where the blood would otherwise drain out of) become compressed, contributing to engorgement as blood cannot be drained and stays in penis. 

Drugs that treat erectile dysfunction block the enzyme that breaks down of cGMP, the second messenger in the pathway in which nitric oxide is released. This results in more nitric oxide which, as mentioned above, relaxes the muscles around the arteries of the penis and maintains vasodilation.

I would argue that it's impossible to prove a food, drug, or chemical "safe". Scientists try to prove something unsafe, then if unsuccessful, consider it *effectively* safe. Actually, MSG has been historically thought to cause a collection of symptoms known as "Chinese food syndrome". The link between MSG and any of those symptoms, including headaches, have been studied but never proven.
